§7§oBewitchment is a mod focused on natural magic and demons.

It provides some player tools.

The mod has a basic support of automation, but it is not the best, so custom multiblocks will eventually replace many of its base machines.
§7§oYou should farm these plants! They will be used quite a lot in bewitchment!

§7§oThe witches oven uses ME to craft! Place it near the witches altar!

JEI will tell you the recipes done by the witches oven!

§7§oThe spinning wheel uses ME to craft! Place it near the witches altar!

JEI will tell you the recipes done by the spinning wheel!

§7§oPlace on top of fire, lava, or a magma block, and near a witches altar.

To start every recipe in the cauldron, place a water bucket inside. If the water stays in the cauldron too long, it will evaporate!

JEI will show the required ingredients for recipes and brews! 

To craft using the cauldron, drop in the required items after the water starts boiling! If a recipe was done correctly, the output will pop out automatically! Make sure you drop each ingredient quickly, otherwise the recipe won't complete.

To make brews, drop a mandrake root, and drop a combination of the desired brew items (JEI will show). You can add gunpowder at the end to make it splashable! Right click the cauldron with empty bottles to collect the potions!

§7§oThe witches altar is how you generate magical energy (ME) in bewitchment!

The structure for the altar is a 3x2 table, and it can be made by any type of altar. Right click the structure with a vanilla carpet to form the altar!

The altar generates energy passively. Right clicking the altar with an empty hand will tell you the available energy, as well as the maximum energy for the altar. Most mechanics in bewitchment use ME to run!

The amount of diverse nature (crops, trees, flowers) will set the maximum ME. The more different plants you have, the higher the maximum energy in the altar!

You can place statues around the altar, or particular artifacts on the altar to add multipliers to ME rate and amount. These will show up when searching 'witches altar' in JEI.

§7§oThe distillery uses ME to craft! Place it near the witches altar!

JEI will tell you the recipes done by the distillery!
§7§oDragon's blood trees can be found in the overworld in a special villager house, or they can be traded with alchemist villagers.

§7§oPlace the crystal ball near a witch's altar.

Right clicking it will consume 500 ME from the altar, and give you buffs!

§7§oChalk is used to draw rituals to produce special effects, summon mobs, or obtain items.

Rituals require an active altar nearby to function.

Right click the ground with chalk to draw runes.

If a ritual requires items, right click them on the center rune!

There are three tiers of rituals, corresponding to the three colors of chalk! 

The middle chalk is always yellow! Right click it to start the ritual!

The following quests list all rituals and what they do! JEI will list how to draw them!

The notable ones are marked as (USEFUL).
§7§oThe codex infernalis unlocks the demonic rituals!

§7§oClick the bottled frostfire on a block to start a cold fire! This will not go out.

Drop iron into the cold fire to make cold iron!
§7§oBottled fires are used as reagents and mechanics for rituals and recipes.
By investing a in more alchemicallly-infused materials, I can make the transmutation portable, and even use it as a work table on the go. Very useful!

§7§oPlace above a ritual altar (4 blocks between altar and linker) to move the effects of a ritual elsewhere.

Place another anchor where you want your ritual to be active, and link the two anchors with a linking tool.

§7§oThis is part of a multiblock.

Right click the ritual altar with a sextant to see a preview of the multiblock.

Place an attuned celestial crystal on the formed altar to produce a special effect. Some are very powerful!

The quests for each attunement will list the ritual effects!

§7§oCollector crystals are used in a variety of applications.

They can be linked to an altar to boost starlight levels.

They can be linked to a ritual using the same attunement to boost the effect of the altar.

By building a structure around the crystal (see preview) it can be used to increase its boosting effect further.
§7§oThis table requires a different multiblock structure!

§7§oThis block is part of a multiblock.

Right click with a sextant to see a multiblock preview.

Right click the infuser with a resonating wand to activate the recipe.

The infuser will only work if all 12 of the spaces in the multiblock are filled with liquid starlight.

Every time the infuser crafts, liquid starlight has a chance of disappearing. 

The containment chalice will provide liquid starlight instead of consuming it from the multiblock. You can pipe it in from the bottom using any fluid pipe!
§7§oRight click while in the Dreadlands to open a portal to Omothol.
§7§oFound at coordinates 0,0 in Omothol.

§7§oThe everfull urn automatically refills crucibles nearby.

This also works with bewitchment crucibles.

§7§oSmelteries are used to make essentia out of items. To see what essentia a given item will produce, you can check the JEI tab for essentia, or press shift while hovering over an item in JEI.

A smeltery works like a furnace, where it needs fuel, which can be automatically inputted from the bottom, to function.

To function properly, a smeltery needs at least one alembic placed on top. If an alembic is not present, all that is smelted will be tuned into flux.

When an item with essentia is smelted, it will be turned into an essentia slurry, shown as a purple bar on the left of the smeltery interface. If an alembic is present, the slurry will be transferred as essentia to the alembic.

Essentia can be collected from the alembic using phials, or you can place a filling essentia transfuser to automatically push essentia to nearby jars.

All operations done by the smeltery will produce a bit of flux, so be careful! Mithrillium tier and above will not make any flux!
§7§oDoes not produce any flux
§7§oDoes not produce any flux, and has a 120% yield
§7§oDoes not produce any flux, and has a 150% yield

§7§oWhile for most situations essentia transfusers are better, for some of the multiblock automations you may want to use essentia pipes.

Essentia tubes only transport one essentia at a time, but multiple essentias can be in the same line.

The valve can be used to switch lines on and off.

The restricted tube can be used to make an output lower priority.

The directional tube only works one-way.

The filter can be used to allow passage of only one essentia. Right click with a phial of the desired type to set its whitelist.

The buffer can be used for intermediate storage of up to 8 essentias. This way multiple types can run through the same line.

§7§oJars are used to store essentia similarly to how tanks are used to store fluids.

To fill a jar, you can use phials, or you can directly click them on essentia containers.

Right clicking a jar with a label will whitelist the essentia it's currently storing so that no other essentia can enter, even after the jar has been emptied. This can be used for essentia storage systems.

There are multiple tiers of jars, each with a different capacity:

Warded: 250
§7§oVoid: 250 + void excess (makes flux)
§7§oBrass: 275
§7§oThaumium: 350
§7§oMithrillium: 1000

§7§oEssentia transfusers are the best way to move essentia around!

Place them on essentia machines, and they automatically move essentia to/from jars nearby.

Filling = from machines to jars

Emptying = from jars to machines
§7§oAdaminite: 2000 (cannot store vitium)
§7§oMithminite: 4000

§7§oHere you can find explanations and tutorials on all of the ways of making infinite resources!

§fIt is clear that, in order to achieve my goals, I need to CREATE!
Luckily, there are a lot of ways of generating matter using science, magic, and a combination of both.
I will keep track of the various methods to generate matter 'ex nihilo' in this chapter.
betterquesting:10.name:8: I need more! A lot More!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
§7§oYes, automatich!

§fThe mechanized coop automatically produces chicken drops from their spawn eggs.

§7§oThe following quests will guide you through bee breeding.

Bees can get complex, but they are also quite powerful.

If you are getting started with bees, make sure to follow these quests!

§fbees are cool
bees are cool!
bees are cool!!!

§o§7§oHere are the best EMC farms for the modpack!

§fAlchemy is a great science, and it allows for the replication and conversion of objects that possess EMC.
This is the easiest way of making matter, but unfortunately, not everything has EMC...

§7§oDo you want to make lots and lots of nether starts, come this way!

§fAlkahestry is a weird art, some may call it a pallid imitation of EMC alchemy, yet, it has its advantages.
The Tome of Arcana is pretty good too!

§7§oThe following quests show the available options for mob farming, as well as woot and deep mob learning!

Mob farms can be extremely powerful in this pack if used effectively, be sure to start early!

§7§oThe following quests list all methods available for plant and tree farming!

See the green revolution section for methods to make your plants faster and better!

§fPlants and trees are extremely useful, so I will need lots of ways to ensure a steady supply of vegetarian goodies.

§7§oThe following quests will list methods to speed up plant growth, and how to level up your seeds with agricraft!

See the r/notjusttrees quest for info on farming automation!

§7§oThe following quests list methods used to automate mining resources!

§fSo many minerals...
If only there was a way to prevent mining trips every few hours...

§7§oThe following quests show how to deal with and farm chickens!

§fGenetically modified chickens, because why the f..k not...

§7§oNesting pens can be used to automate chickens in a straightforward matter! And there is a chance for a few special drops!

The net can be used to put chickens in the nesting pens.

§fA nesting pen can increase the eggification of chickens. Not the best, but it'll do for a bit.
A henhouse provided with hay can collect chicken drops in a radius around it.

Cursed earth, coming from withers, in absence of light, creates monsters at incredibly fast rates.
A grinder kills monsters making essence as a byproduct, and its range can be upgraded using addons, depending on the size of the cursed earth parch.
This is a technique earth scientist developed after global warming almost wiped out humanity.
Essence is essentially undifferentiated stem cellular matter, produced from decaying corpses.
Stem cells can be made into anything... Well, almost anything...

Want a synthetic source of flavorless food?
Then this may be what you need...
Oh and there's pink slime!

Boys! The plan is simple!
Use a lot of energy...make lots of mobs!"

Thaumic magic can be used to replicate monsters?!
No essence needed?!
Creatures can be duplicated with this machine consuming essence, given the programmation provided by an Imprisonment Tool.

For some reason, draconic powers can be used to massively replicate a select set of powerful monsters...
This will come in handy later...
§7§oDropped by most mobs, this is a stackable item form of XP.
Just gonna leave this here!
betterquesting:10.name:8: For the sake of your world, you should do this!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
§7§oWoot lets you build mob farms without spawning mobs. Note, they can get large!

There are 4 tiers of woot farms! Each tier will drop shards of the tier after (tier 1 farm drops tier 1 and 2 shards)!

To start, craft a factory heart and an intern! The intern lets you select a tier, and it will tell you the materials you need to build the woot farm! Clicking the heart with the intern will build the mobfarm!

After the structure is complete, you will have to add some blocks manually. To check is those are correct, right click the factory heart with a ya hammer.

Place the following blocks under the farm, in this exact order from top to bottom, directly under the heart, with a gap of at most 10 blocks: power cell, factory importer, factory exporter.

To farm a specific mob with woot, you need a bound ender shard. Hit a mob with it, and kill it after to bind your shard (it will start glowing).

Use the bound shard to craft a controller, and place it on top of the block behind the factory heart!

§fCreating creatures and monsters is cool and all, but making them digitally is better (for chunks and fps).
Also, it seems like these factories can produce things that normally seem to only come from my sword!

§7§oWoot upgrades are placed on the upgrade casings.

For multiple levels of the same upgrade, you should stack them in order, with the lower tier at the bottom, and the higher at the top.

§fDigital factories can be upgraded, weeeeeee!
Some stygian iron...and essence is now easy!

§7§oTo farm mob drops with Deep Mob Learning (Evolution), you need a simulation chamber, a loot fabricator, and a steady supply of polymer clay (which has EMC), as well as a data model.

To function, a simulation chamber needs a data model that has been configured to a mob.

To configure a model, you need to place one for the mob you want to farm into the deep learner. Then you want to slay a certain number that mob to activate the model, while holding the learner into your hotbar.

The more mobs you slay, the higher the tier of the model. The higher the tier, the better.

Placing a model in the simulation chamber will produce pristine matter, which is consumed in loot fabricators to farm specific mob drops.

§fA simulation chamber that has been programmed with a data model consumes polymer clay to produce mob matter.
The loot fabricator uses pristine matter to produce mob drops.

§7§oThe digital mob agonizer is a very effective way to produce essence for a blood altar.

Place one next to a blood altar, and use the altar linker to bind it.

The digital mob agonizer needs a data model, and a steady supply of matter, and it will automatically add life essence to the altar.

Multiple agonizers can be connected to the same altar!

§fSmaller digital factories, more life essence!
Digital factories, digital monsters, real life essence!
Thanks to the power of entropy manipulation, I can build one-block mobfarms with extremely high rates!
A digital factory is the best way to make certain things, powerful things...
The power of the Aevitas constellation makes plant growth really fast, may need to look into it...
The Moon Harvest blood ritual can be used to infuse life essence into plants, and crops too!
The lamp of growth is a fairly inexpensive way of speeding up the growth of plants.
Sprinklers can increase a plant's growth speed by acting as automatic watering cans, when provided with water.
The powers of inferium can also allow for the speeding up of plant growth, nice!
Things get W I D E R!
Things get W I D E R!
Things get W I D E R!
No refills needed!
Get water, put on plants, plants go *growing sound*
Entropy manipulation is a powerful thing, and it works on plants too!

Can things get any better? Yes they can!
If you know how to get CREATIVE...

§7§oCrop sticks can be used to duplicate or improve crops.

Only plants placed on crop sticks can be improved. Crops have three stats: growth, gain and strength. All stats have a level ranging from 1 to 10.

All planted crops start at level 1/1/1, and become much better when levelled to 10/10/10. 

If you right click crop sticks with crop sticks, you make crossing crop sticks.

If crossing crop sticks are placed next to planted crop sticks, the plant will spread, sharing its stats.

If two or more planted crops are placed around double crop sticks, the resulting plant may come out with better stats.

The seed analyzer can be used to look at a given plant's stats. 

If you want to challenge yourself with some boolean logic, integrated dynamics can be used to automate the process of making 10/10/10 seeds.

§7§oStone and nether essences can be used to create ores with Mythic properties.

One mineral makes one ore...

One ore makes multiple minerals, especially if you use an industrial grinder!

This process can be looped for exponential yield (granted that you have enough essence).

Works with Rupee, Arlemite, Realmite, Rosite, Limonite, Netherite, Bloodgem, Emberstone, Runium, Ascended Jade, Ascended Sapphire,, Ascended Amethyst.
The glacial precipitator uses water to produce various ice-related items.

§7§oA builder, programmed with a quarry card, is very good at ruining landscapes!

In this configuartion, this machine will automatically excavate large regions, collecting all blocks it escavates.

Place an inventory on top of the builder to collect drops.

§7§oUsing a quantum quarry is optional, but it may be good depending on your situation!

The quantum quarry produces ground drops from a hypothetical dimension, thus limiting the environmental impact of quarrying.
Specific biomes can be configured in the multiblock to target particular minerals or ground materials.

The igneous extruder passively produces rocks by using water and lava.
Upgrades can be used to reduce fluid usage.

§7§oVoid miners are multiblocks that automatically generate resources at random.

The void resource miner's main use is mica, which is used in some useful recipes.

You can upgrade your resource miner to other tiers, but it's not as important, until you reach later stages in the game!

§fDo I really need this many rocks?!
Well, I can make them from nothing...

§7§oVoid miners are multiblocks that automatically generate resources at random.

Void ore miners are very good at collecting all minerals. 

The higher the tier, the better the drops, and you will unlock additional resources!

It is a good idea to start levelling up your void ore miners ASAP!

§fLet's make things more environmental (and lag) friendly!
And I can make litherite too!
Better virtual minerals, better yield!
Better virtual minerals, better yield!
Better virtual minerals, better yield!
Better virtual minerals, better yield!
Better virtual minerals, better yield!

§7§oThis modpack has a lot of different machines and crafting mechanics, here you can see explanations and tutorials for each!

§fThere are a lot of machines and processes to automate, I will leave this space to write down some info on each of them...

§7§oThe automation upgrade automatically combines a princess and a drone after the queen is done. This means you can automate combs passively!

You should do this to automate rocky and dripping combs, as well as others later in progression!

§fTired of moving princesses, well you don't have to!

§7§oThe industrail apiary has two functions:

1. Combines a princess and a drone into a queen! You should only put bees of the same species in here, unless you know what you are doing!

2. If you put a queen in the apiary, it will slowly produce combs, drones, and a princess (guaranteed if pristine, only use pristine). 

Every bee will need flowers to work, the portable analyzer will tell you what flowers to use!

If you get an error, it means you need to change biome or humidity settings! The upgrades in the attached quests can be used to get rid of these arrors.

If you want to automate a particular type of comb, you can use the automation upgrade!

The industrial apiary can be tick accelerated using time in a bottle!

§fTechnology makes everything better, waaaaaay better.

§7§oIf you are just getting started with forestry, you should not use the apiary! Use the industrial apiary instead!

The apiary will produce bee offspring following mendelian genetics. Given a dominant gene A, and a recessive gene a, if the queen is AA and the drone is aa, the offspring will have a 25% chance of being AA (expressing A), 50% chance of being Aa (expressing A), 25% chance of being aa (expressing a).

§fAn apiary is used to get honey combs from bees (no really?!), but it's not a really good way of doing it.

§7§oWant more drones? More flowers? These upgrades can help!

§fMore useful apiary stuff!

§7§oIf you get errors in the industrial apiary GUI, use these upgrades to change the biome or humidity!

§7§fWrong humidity, well no problem!

§7§oIf you get errors in the industrial apiary GUI, use these upgrades to change the biome or humidity!

§IInstead of moving my bees around, I can just emulate biomes from the comfort of my §fhome!

§7§oThe genetic transposer has two main functions.

First, it can be used to duplicate gene samples, combine a blank one with an imprinted one to duplicate it! This is how you can farm the ingredients to craft the torcherino!

Second, you can combine genetic samples into templates, these will be used to customize your bees!

NOTE: templates do not need to have all 12 genes! You can make templates with even one chromosome!

§7§oAs you can see using a portable analyzer, bees have a variety of genes! Some are good, and some are, well, not great.

The genetic sampler is the first step in making your bees better! It takes bees, and has a chance of producing gene samples from a given bee.

For each bee species that has a desirable gene (the best ones are listed in the following quests), you can dump excess drones into the sampler, until you obtain the gene samples you desire!

See next quests for more info on how to transfer good genes to other bees!

§fBy consuming drones, which can be endlessly bred, I can isolate specific gene traits. Some of them (but just some) are very useful!

§7§oWARNING: Bee genetics and breeding can get very complex, unless you know what you are doing, you should follow these three main rules to keep things simple:

1. A princess and a drone, when combined, make a queen. If the drone and princess are the same species, the queen will be the same species. If you combine princess and drone from different species, you can create new ones (JEI will guide you with this). You should only use the advanced mutatron to create new bee species!

2. A queen makes a princess and several drones, as well as combs, depending on the species (again JEI will guide you). You should only use the industrial apiary to run bees of the same species!

3. Ignoble stock bees are bad, pristine bees are good! You should not use ignoble queens/princesses. There are ways to make ignobles work, but the methods are more advanced.

If you know what you are doing, bees follow the rules of Mendelian genetics. Every bee trait has a dominant and recessive gene, the portable analyzer will give you the genetic makeup of a given bee! Breeding bees to select specific traits can get you much faster and more efficient bees!

§fBee genetics are surprisingly complex, not surprised they took over the universe!
The bee analyzer will help me to keep track of bee genes at the cost of a little honey.
Rock hives are a good source of princesses, if only there was a way to make an endless supply of them...
At the cost of DNA and Protein, I can even make new bees from scratch, including hard-to-get princesses!

§7§oGiven a template from the genetic transposer, you can use the imprinter to modify a bee's genes.

If you want to imprint a queen, you will have to imprint both a princess and a drone, and the resulting queen will be guaranteed to have the desired genes.

WARNING: bees have a (low) chance of being turned into genetic waste, so be careful about imprinting princesses. If you want to avoid losing a princess, imprint a lot of drones, and reiteratively combine them into queens until you have all the desired genes.

§fCan I make my bees Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger? Heck yeah I can!
Pristine > Ignoble

§7§oThe advanced mutatron is the easiest way of making a new species! This should be the main and only way to make new bees!

Make sure you use pristine princesses only!

Combine the right princess and drone to create a queen of a new species! JEI lists all bee breeding combinations!

Once you make a queen, you should put it in an industrial apiary!

§fNo variance, no problem!

§7§oYou should upgrade to the advanced mutatron ASAP! No need to use the base one, unless you know what you are doing!

The mutagen produces makes mutagen, which is used in the mutatron.

§fAt the cost of some radioactive material, and a bunch of power, bees can be easily bred into new species. Variance may still play a role, though...
Excess drones? More mana!
Using a tome of arcana, emerald can be converted into experience bottles, this is awesome!

§7§oThe Tome of Alkahestry, in most situations, is a worse version of the philosopher stone, but its ability to replicate nether stars makes it very useful.

The tome is charged when shapelessly crafted with redstone.

If the tome has enough charge, it will duplicate nether stars when shapelessly crafted with them.

A crafter in ExtC mode will let you make a very cheap and effective nether star farm, provided with a steady supply of redstone!

In order to endlessly produce matter using EMC, the knowledge of three devices is needed.
Firsly, collectors generate EMC from light. Glowstone are the better source for these purposes. The more glowstone blocks surrounding a collector, the faster EMC will be produced.
Secondly, Relays act like like EMC batteries, and are able to transmit this type of power to/from adjacent blocks. This means that the energy from multiple collectors can be funnled into a single block using a Relay.
Finally, condensers can use EMC provided by adjacent relays and collectors to duplicate a given item.
A condenser, to remain accessible with maximum efficiency, still has five free faces, and so do relays...
§7§oThe alchemical catalyst is a valuable EMC item. It can be farmed using a botanic condenser, or with the EMBee!
Better Relays, better Collectors, better EMC!

§7§oEMC loops exploit recipes where the output of a given recipe has a higher value than the sum of the inputs!

Meatballcraft's intended EMC loops are the ones using Dragon Hearts, so if you discover more, please report it!

Four blaze rods have a combined EMC value of 6144, a diamond has a value of 8192!
The crafter from RFTools can be used to automate making diamonds from blaze rods! Make sure you set it to ExtC mode to keep the dragon heart!
The diamonds can be piped into a condenser MK2 to make more blaze rods than you started with!
Pipe the blaze rods from the condenser back into the crafter, to complete the loop!
You can dump the excess blaze rods into another condenser to farm any EMC item you want!


§fWhile basic Condensers are very good when connected to Relays or Collectors, if items are fed into this baseline version, things get a bit awkward...
The upgraded Condenser is designed for item duplication from outside inputs (E.G. cobble gen, crop farms).
There are some very good farms that passively produce items with high EMC values
Red Matter > Dark Matter

§7§oEMC links are a way to extract and insert EMC into your personal network (your transmutation tablet).

The basic energy EMC link is used to add EMC to your network, you can only input items into it, but cannot pull them out!

The personal EMC link is like a condenser that takes EMC from your own network. See next quests for upgrades on the personal link!

WARNING: DO not attach EMC links directly to AE2 buses, this will cause a lot of lag!
§7§oWorks like a personal EMC link, but it can output 9 items at the same time!

§7§oBonsai pots let you passively generate EMC for your personal EMC network.

Place a bonsai pot in a loaded chunk, and it will automatically add EMC at a constant rate.

The higher the tier, the faster EMC will be added!
§7§oWorks like a personal EMC link, but it can output 54 items at the same time!

§7§oWhile there are other, more compact ways of farming plants and trees, large material-based farms can be used for more than trees, and they have really good yield.

Multiblock farms can be programmed for a variety of purposes. The best use is to make peat, which is used in a lot of recipes later on.

To program a multiblock farm, you need a circuit, which is programmed using a soldering iron!

The higher the circuit tier, the more things at the same time can be farmed (up to 4).

§7§oThe plant sower is used to plant up to 9 different types of plants.
The gatherer can automatically harvest plants, producing sludge as a byproduct.
§7§oThe emerald electron tube allows for the farming of crop sticks!

§7§oThis is not the best option, but it is an option!

Some plants don't need to be broken and replaced to produce drops, and this device takes advantage of this to harvest crops without the need for replanting.

§7§oThe sludge refiner uses sludge to create various earthy materials, including some quite useful stuff!
Conductive powder is a very interesting byproduct...

§7§oThe obsidian electron tube is used to configure these large farms to produce peat.

A peat multiblock farm needs a steady supply of bog earth.
Farming stations are a relatively expensive, but very versatile, way to automatically farm both crops and trees.
§7§oThe phytogenic insolator is a one-block plant farm that requires some sort of fertilizer to produce both crop and tree drops (if upgraded with an arboreal extractor).

Latex can be extracted from a wood log placing a tree fluid extractor next to it.
Multiple extractors can be placed around a single log.
Some sort of automatic placer can be used to replenish consumed logs once they are depleted by the extractors.
The resonator uses grid power to infuse some materials with grid power, which can be passively produced from a wide array of sources.
Turns solids into fluids!!

Makes alloys accepting up to three materials.
And smelts things too!
A device that fills (empties) fluid containers.

High pressure = better
For making steam from solid and liquid fuels.
Oil separation is truly a wonderful process!

Smelting.
With.
Electricity.

The smeltery is built out of seared bricks placed in a cuboid shell, with no roof and no edges.
The controller is where the interface is accessible, and acts as an item input (for automation).
The tank is the smeltery's lava (or other hot fluid) input.
Drains act as fluid output ports. Faucets and fluid pipes connect to drains.
Tables and basins are placed under faucets to accept molten fluids. Basins turn them into blocks, tables can be used with a variety of casts (gold is better).
Faucets output fluids when clicked, or with a redstone signal.
Redstone clocks and timers are good for automating faucet extraction, if you don't want to use pipes.

Laser go *zzzz
Crystal go *whooosh
Right click with a redstone torch to swap between deactivation and pulse mode.
Place next to a pressure plate in pulse mode to zap whatever is placed on the plate for simple automation.
The latex processing unit combines latex with RF and water to make tiny dry rubber.

At the cost of some grid powewr and some RF, this machine can harness the power of enchanting to create some pretty cool things.
Just like an enchanting table, this requires some external boost (from bookshelves, magical wood, etc.)

Turns fluids into solids!
No way!

Pulverizes things producing chance drops.
Grinding balls can be used to increase yield.
A crafting table with extra steps!

To make all of the chipsets.
And a dope laser show!
Recipes are encoded by the assembly table, powered by surrounding lasers, the more the better!
Dries things, and accepts pipe inputs and outputs.
Four display stands, placed around the empowerer two blocks away.
Sludge, which is a byproduct of the Plant Gatherer, can be reprocessed in this machine to produce various terrous materials, includeing mycelium and some other goodies...

Trading is an act between two living things, but it doesn't have to be like that thanks to this device, which allows to automate this process.
A villager captured using a Mob Imprisonment Tool can be mercilessly forced to spend the rest of its life as an emerald farm!
The enchantment extractor can split a book with multiple enchants into separate ones, and extract single enchants from an enchanted item.

In search of some fluid to put into an ender combustion generator?
Plant scraps would work pretty well here!

Protein as an energy source?
Sure, just take some animal meat!

Slices and Splices organic and inorganic things together consuming the durability of an axe and shears.
Durability is not consumed if the tools are unbreakable!
Infuses souls from soul vials into items!
Dissolves solid items into fluids to make other fluids! (did you really need quest text to figure that out?!?)
Centrifuges honey combs into their components.
Makes biomass from a variety of inputs.
Seed oil, honey, and a few other things...

Infuses water into items.
Basically a worse fluid transposer (but don't tell him that).
Let's distill something!
3x3 crafting, and glass
Bro you want to see my $700 juicer?
Because alcohol
Because alcohol
Smart molten metal output, can be upgraded to fulfill a variety of needs.

The Pure Daisy is used to transform the 8 blocks around it.
This can be easily automated using block placers and breakers, or by using formation and annihilation planes in a AE2 subnet.

The wizardry Combiner uses the powers of wizardry to make powerful magical artifacts...
...and some other things as well...

The Dragonfire Crucible uses the extreme heat of eternal dragon fire and twilight fire to fuse materials together.
Fire can be passively supplied using fluid transport methods.

The Dragonfire Forge is used to produce fluids using the power of dragon fire.
Multiple of these should be built to passively automate high-heat fluids.
The corrupted library uses artifacts from Iceika and Arcana to fabricate things magically.

The Mana Pool transforms items dropped into it using mana.
An item dropper or a precision hopper can be used to automate the Mana Pool.

§7§oThis multiblock produces flux, so make sure you have ways to clear it up if you automate it!

Right click the structure with salis mundus to form the furnace from the multiblock preview!

Drop items from the top to smelt them, meats have a chance of producing meat nuggets.

This multiblock is used to fabricate circuits and machine parts.
Use holo projector to see multiblock preview.

§7§oA magma block is required underneath the anvil to provide enough heat.

Specific casts can be used for multiple outcomes, so an anvil for each cast is recommended.

Recipe items can be dropped or dispensed directly on the anvil.

§7§oSalt reactors are used to process fission fuels and to heat NaK fluids, which can be used to generate power using a heat exchanger and a turbine.

See the multiblock preview for a preview of the exterior frame of a salt reactor.

To function, a salt reactor needs cooling, done through NaK fluids, and fuel, all of which follow proximity rules similar to fission reactors.

Inside a salt reactor, fluids are transported using coolant heaters (for NaK) and fission vessels (for fuel). These act similarly to fluid pipes, with a few extra rules.

Simpler designs use fuel flowing from end to end, but if fluids can be properly handled, coolants and fission vessels can be placed anywhere within the coolants' rules. 

The rules for a given coolant vessel depend on the fluid flowing through it and are the same as their solid fuel counterpart, e.g. NaK-Redstone filled coolant heaters have the same placement rules as passive redstone coolers.

Right click each face of a vessel and coolant heater with an empty hand to change its input/output mode. Shift right click lets you change the opposite side.

You can place a new vessel with a copy of the settings of a previous vessel by shift right clicking it with a vessel to place (this can bug out unfortunately).

The easiest way to build a salt reactor is to configure a single layer of the interior setup first (starting from the middle block), followed by shift-clicking the next layers, and to build the outside frame at the end.

To connect two vessels (or coolant heaters) they should have FUEL SPREAD (or COOLANT SPREAD) on their exit face, entering a DEFAULT face. 

Touching coolant and fuel lines with different fluids should have DISABLED on touching faces.

To feed fluids from outside a salt reactor, vessels have to be connected to vents, both on the input and output side. 

To connect a vessel (or coolant heater) to the output vent it should have DEPLETED OUT (or HOT COOLANT OUT) on the face touching the vent.

For each of the fuel byproducts required in progression, multiblock previews for interior reactor designs are provided. These will show an individual cross section that can be stacked into any length.

If NaK coolant is absent from inside the reactor, or if fluids cannot freely leave the reactor, it will melt down, making even more radiation. Make sure you are making plenty of coolant, and have a way to circulate it quickly.

Using a heat exchanger, it is possible to fully recycle NaK fluids, allowing for closed-loop designs.

§7§oXnet is a medium-power logistics tool.

It is the recommended way to manage passive automations of lots of different items coming in and out of machines.

It is much more performant than enderIO conduits for item transfer.

Xnet can also be used to mode energy, although the transfer rate may not be high enough for all applications.

Because of a bug with the mod, conduits are still better than Xnet for fluid automation.
§7§oThe thermal energy cell is the basic energy storage block. It can be upgraded into stronger versions using upgrade and conversion kits.
§7§oCapacitor banks can be assembled into multiblocks to increase their storage and transfer rate.

§7§oThe draconic energy core is part of a multiblock that stores energy.

You can activate a multiblock preview after placing down the energy core.

All tiers but the max are craftable (with some effort) in chapter 2!

§7§oFor long term, the draconic energy orb is the best option, and it is craftable in chapter 2.

Until then, large stacks of vibrant capacitor banks will do the trick!
§7§o9x9x9 (perfection)

§7§oEvery Xnet system requires a controller, a connector for each inventory you want to interact with, and network cables to connect them.

The controller requires power, which should come from an external source (flux point my beloved). Do not power your Xnet controller with an Xnet connector, it will cause lag.

For conduits and ducts, each individual connection is handled independently. For Xnet, each connection to other inventories in handled by the controller GUI. 

All inventories that have connectors and valid network cable connections will show up on the controller. You can double click an inventory to see its location in-world.

A single Xnet setup can do up to 8 functions at the same time, described by 8 channels, corresponding to the columns in the GUI.

Each channel can be configured to do:

Energy transfer: set individual inventories as energy inputs or outputs, useful for powering single-block machines that also need item automation.

Item transfer: set individual inventories as inputs or outputs of specific filtered or general items; you can specify what sides to interact with for sided machines like furnaces.

Logic (redstone): you can add sensors (produce redstone if chest has over X amount of item A); additionally, both item and energy channels can receive logic signals to turn on/off their function (move item B if receiving redstone signal); logic (redstone) channels can be colored as well to operate independently.

Fluid transfer: it's bugged, don't use it

RFTools: combined with the storage interface from RFTools, you can make mini AE2 networks.

ComputerCraft Plethora: you can interact with computers.

§7§oEvery Xnet system requires a controller, a connector for each inventory you want to interact with, and network cables to connect them.

Like cables, connectors can be dyed to allow for different setups next to each other.

Connectors are placed on a side of inventories and machines, but they can interact with any side. So you can extract from the bottom while the connector is on the top (if you have to work with sided machines). This can be specified in the controller GUI.

§7§oEvery Xnet system requires a controller, a connector for each inventory you want to interact with, and network cables to connect them.

Cables can be colored if you want to have different Xnet setups next to each other.

§7§oRouting cables and connectors are used to link routers to each other, if for some reason you need even more channels to interact between each other.

Routers connected by routing cables and connectors will work the same way, but using the right side of the GUI as well.

Both local (left) and remote (right) channels can interact with each other, and be unified, as long as they have the same label in the router GUI.

§7§oA router can be used to share functionality between different Xnet setups.

If multiple different Xnet setups are connected to the same router, individual channels can be unified between them.

The left side of the router GUI lists all channels in all Xnet setups attached to the router. If two channels are given the same label in the router, they will start acting as the same channel, split between different Xnet controllers.

§7§oWireless routers and antennas can be used instead of multiple routers being connected by routing cables, if you want to connect Xnet setups, and share channels, wirelessly.

They work like regular routers, but they need energy.

The antenna base is placed on top of the wireless router.

Regular antennas can be placed on top of the antenna base for short distance connections.

Antenna dishes are used for large distance connections instead of antennas.

§7§oApplied Energistics is a high-capability logistics mod.

Alone, it can manage a large part of your base, including item storage, autocrafting, and managing passive automations externally.

Expect to build a massive AE2 network, and likely a ton of small ones too!

The following quests show all tools available in this complex but powerful mod!

§7§oThe ME controller is the heart of every AE2 system.
Each controller can output 8 (basic) to 32 (dense) channels from each side, depending on the tipe of ME cable used.
Only one controller is allowed for a given network. Multiple controllers can be combined to form multiblocks.

§7§oME storage busses use one channel to connect to an inventory. Any items contained in the inventory will become part of the network, and can be seen in the terminals.

Extract only mode makes it so you can see the storage in your terminal, but the network will not store new items into the storage.

Insert only mode makes it so you will not be able to see the storage in your terminal, but it will force the network to move items into the storage.

§7§oThe use of this bus is discouraged!

The crafting card can be added to interfaces and export buses to force craft an item if it's not present in storage.
§7§oIncreases the number of configurable slots in export, import, and storage buses.

§7§oThe ME dual interface can store patters for recipes that contain both items and fluids.

Fluids will have to be moved with conduits or other fluid transport.

§7§oThe automation interface is not recommended for autocrafting, but it is a cheap option.

Using package crafters is recommended!

Place the automation upgrade on top of any extended crafting table to encode a single recipe for automation.

If placed adjacent to an unpackager that has been configured with the same recipe (you will need a packager too), the recipe can be automated similarly.

§7§oThe package crafters for each extended crafting table are placed around an unpackager, and they work like molecular assemblers for extended recipes.

You can place multiple package crafters around an unpackager (up to six) to parallelize recipes and faster processing.

Since each packager/unpckager pair holds up to 20 recipes, you can have setups that handle 20 recipes for each table.

§7§oPlace the ender package crafter next to a properly configured unpackager to autocraft with it!

The more ender alternators you place around the crafter (you need at least one), the faster it will craft!

§7§oME glass cables are the simplest way to transfer channels to make a AE2 network. 
They can carry up to 8 channels, but they do not display how many are currently used.

In general, you should use smart cables instead!
§7§oSmart cables can carry up to 8 channels, and they display how many are being used.

§7§oThe ME drive is used to store storage cells.

Storage cells are like chests that contain items/fluids.

Each cell stores 63 different stacks, and a certain amount of items depending on the tier.

The following quests list all tiers of cells!
§7§oDense cables carry up to 32 channels, and they display how many are in use.

§7§oSmart cables that can fit in the same block space as other conduits.

Good for compactness!

§7§oDense cables that can fit in the same block space as other conduits.

Good for compactness!

§7§oNormally, when working with patterns for 'normal' recipes, you just need one interface.
To encode these recipes, you need two blocks! 

The packager is the first! You should put your first package recipe holder in a packager.

These can be placed anywhere in your AE2 network, but for organization it's a good idea to put them close to their respective unpackager.

§7§oYou should use a packager/unpackager pair. Place the combination package crafter adjacent to the unpackager.

To perform recipes, the package combination crafters needs marked pedestals around it, one for each individual item!
§7§oWorks like a molecular assembler, where inputs such as filled buckets will be treated directly as fluids.

§7§oThe fluid interface lets you encode processing recipes with fluid inputs and outputs!

Place a pattern into the interface to add the recipe to they network.

With some machines, you may need to use conduits or other pipes to extract and insert!

§7§oThe interface has two functions, see the section on network I/O for an explanation on the other functionality.

The slots at the bottom on an interface GUI can be used to store patterns. Each pattern encodes a recipe or processing step.

If the interface is touching a molecular assembler, it will perform a crafting recipe.

If the interface is next to a machine (furnace, pulverizer, chest, etc) it will perform a processing recipe.

Some machines don't auto output, so you will have to use conduits or other transfer pipes to put machine outputs back into the interface.

§7§oTo encode recipes that have more than 9 inputs at once, you cannot use the pattern terminal. Instead, you should use the package recipe encoder to set package recipe holders (these are your patterns).

For each set of recipes, you should encode TWO recipe holders. Each recipe holder can do up to 20 recipes, categorized as processing, and as each of the extended crafting mechanics.

To encode a recipe, you can do it similarly to how a pattern terminal works! The plus sign in JEI will work!

You should NOT encode multiple recipe types (processing, basic table, etc) on the same recipe holder pair!

Make sure you save your recipe holders!

§7§oPatters are used to store crafting and processing recipes so that your AE2 network can autocraft!

Patterns are encoded in the pattern terminal (any type).

To perform a recipe, place a pattern into an interface. If this is set up correctly, you will be able to requiest automatic crafting of items from your crafting terminal!

If the interface is touching a molecular assembler, it will perform a crafting recipe.

If the interface is next to a machine (furnace, pulverizer, chest, etc) it will perform a processing recipe.

§7§oMolecular assemblers are used to perform crafting recipes.

The more molecular assemblers are touching an interface, the faster it will craft.

Acceleration cards can be used on molecular assemblers!
§7§oThe import buses are used to input items from external inventories into your AE2 network.

§7§oThe export buses are used to move items/fluids/essentia from the AE2 network to external inventories.

An export bus pointing into a chest will put items into the chest.

§7§oCrafting storage lets you store the information for a given autocrafting task, the bigger the crafting storage, the bigger the craft.

Multiple storages can be stacked in a crafting processing unit.

§7§oCo-Processing units let you parallelize some of the intermediate steps in crafting recipes!

The more co-processing units, the more parallelization.

§7§oTo access your AE2 network wirelessly, you will first need a security terminal and a wireless access point.

The security terminal is for linking your wireless terminal to a network. Simply insert your wireless terminal and take it right back out. The wireless access point is for extending the range of your wireless terminal. 

By default, there is a 16 block range, but this can be increased by giving the wireless access point booster cards. This will exponentially increase both the range and the power consumption of the device. The maximum is 64 booster cards for a range of 544 blocks and 8.21 kRF per tick.

§7§oBig energy cell!

§7§oProvides infinite energy to your AE2 network.

If you have this, you won't need to give power to your controllers and energy acceptors!

§7§oThe crafting terminal has a crafting table that lets you access your entire storage system with JEI + sign compatibility!

You can import recipes from JEI. If an item shows as blue in the JEI recipe preview, you can middle click on it to automatically autocraft it!

§7§oThe fluid terminal lets you access all fluids stored in your AE2 storage system.

Use buckets and other fluid storage to extract fluids from the terminal!

WARNING: if you plan to manage fluids with AE2, you should use a subnet to store and move fluids, and prevent access from the main network. This will reduce lag by a lot!

§7§oThe interface terminal lets you access all of the interfaces in your ME network.

You can use this terminal to place patterns into interfaces!

If you name your interfaces, you can search them by name!
§7§oWorks like the crafting terminal, but it's an arcane workbench!

§7§oThe essentia terminal lets you see all the thaumcraft essentia stored in your AE2 storage system.

Use phials to extract essentia from the terminal!

§7§oWorks like the pattern terminal, but can encode recipes with fluids as well!

You should have both a fluid pattern terminal and a pattern terminal!

§7§oThe ME pattern terminal lets you encode recipes into patterns for autocrafting.

Patterns have two modes: 'Crafting Pattern' works for molecular assembler recipes, 'Processing Pattern' mode works for any interface-machine interaction!

Press R on an item in JEI to add it as a recipe. Click and drag items in JEI to add them as recipes manually!
§7§oThe extended processing pattern terminal works like a pattern terminal, but has 16 inputs and 3 output slots!

§7§oWireless connectors are a lower-scale version of the quantum bridge. 

They have a very high energy cost, growing quadratically with distance. They will not work across dimensions.

Only one network requires power for both to function.

Use the setup kit to link two connectors together.

§7§oThanks to Fox and StaffiX for the help!

§7§oThe quantum bridge is a multiblock that allows you to do two things: 

Transfer 32 channels wirelessly over infinite distances and between dimensions.
Obtain a pair of entangled singularties and a pair of quantum bridges that you would like to connect. Place an entangled singularity in each quantum bridge to link them.
Both sides of the connection should have a power input, either from the Controller or from an Energy Acceptor, and both should have at least one Energy Cell.
You can use these to run p2p subnets, but they may misbehave depending on the complexity of your subnet.

Infinitely expand the range of your wireless terminals.
Connect a quantum bridge to the network which you would like to access wirelessly. Insert the quantum link card into the quantum bridge. Note that this will prevent you from inserting an entangled singularity because a quantum bridge can only have one function at a time. This also replaces the need for a wireless access point.

Thanks to Fox for the Help!

§7§oThe network tool lets you see how many components are connected to your AE2 network, and how much power it needs to run!

§7§oFlux Networks are used to transfer energy wirelessly, and are the preferred energy transfer method in the pack.

To create your own Flux Network, you need a Controller. You can specify the name of teh network and a color in the Controller GUI. Each Flux Networks machine will have to be bound to a network to function.

Flux Plugs are used to move energy from a source to a network.

Flux Points are used to move energy from a network to a set of machines.

Flux Storage is used to include a buffer of energy in a network. If you have to transfer large amounts of RF/t, Storage is required to prevent energy cutouts.

It is recommended to still use other energy transfer methods to limit the use of Flux Plugs, as using too many can cause lag. If you want to power a machine wall, for example, use a single Flux Point, and Energy Conduits of the appropriate size to power the machines.

Your base should have two Flux Networks, one to move energy from your generators to a centralized energy storage (eventually the Draconic Energy Orb), one to move energy from storage to all of your machines.

§7§oThis pack may need you to set up some elaborate automations. Here are some useful redstone gadgets you may need!

§7§oBundled cables let you transmit multiple colors of insulated wires in the same line, both in wire and framed wire version!

If you connect two or more colors of insulated wires to the same bundled cable, each color will be transmitted independently with no interference!

§7§oBoth wires and framed wires have insulated counterparts.

Insulated wires of the same color will connect to each other.

Insulated wires of different colors will not connect, letting you run multiple redstone lines in compact spaces.

Insulated wires cannot receive redstone directly, you will need a regular red alloy wire to attach to machines or levers.

For even more compactness, use bundled wires!

§7§oFramed red alloy works like red alloy wire, but it occupies block spaces, making it possible to be in air, with no need for pillar blocks.

To connect a red alloy wire to a framed red alloy wire, they need to be placed in the same block space.

§7§oRed alloy wire is like vanilla redstone, but better!

Signal from red alloy wire will decay after 255 blocks instead of 15, meaning that you can make your redstone lines as long as you want!

Red alloy wire can also be placed on walls, allowing for compact contraptions!

§7§oThe sequencer produces redstone signals at a constant interval from each of its sides, in a clockwise and counterclockwise fashion.

Right click the gate to set the time interval between each side.

Right click with a screwdriver to flip the direction of the loop (counterclockwise to clockwise and vice versa).

§7§oThis gate produces a redstone pulse every time it receives a redstone signal of any length.

Any time the input redstone goes from off to on, the output will pulse.

§7§oThe timer will produce a pulse of redstone at configurable intervals, which can be configured by right clicking.

Timers are tuned off with a redstone signal.

Timers can get laggy if they run constantly, so make sure to incorporate some sort of control to turn them off!

§7§oThis gate lets you control how a single output connects to two inputs.

The side with the taller torch is the output.

The side opposite to it is the control side.

If the control side is on, the gate will only trasfer signals from the side to the left of the control.

If the control side is off, the gate will only transfer signals from the side to the right of the control.

§7§oThis gate lets you add red alloy wire levels.

The side with a torch is the output, and the three inputs are summed.

§7§oThis gate lets you delay a redstone signal by 2, 4, 6, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 ticks, and it resets red alloy levels to 255.

Right click the repeater to change the delay.

§7§oThis gate has two outputs, a setting input, and a lock input.

The outputs have the taller torches.

The setting input has the shorter torch.

The lock input has just redstone.

When the lock input receives a redstone signal, the output replicates what the setting input indefintely, even after it changes.

If the setting is on, pulsing the lock turns the output on.

If the setting is off, pulsing the lock turns the output off.

§7§oThis gate has two inputs and four outputs.

The sides with torches are just outputs, while the sides with just redstone are both inputs and outputs.

When one input receives a pulse, both itself and its corresponding output will tun on indefinitely.

When the other input receives a pulse, the same will happen on the other side.

You can use buffer gates on the inputs to turn them into just inputs.

§7§oThis gate has twom inputs and two outputs.

The sides with redstone lines are the inputs, and they can be used interchangeably.

One of the outputs will be always on, and one will be always off. Receiving a pulse from one of the inputs will invert the two outputs.

§7§oThis gate lets you control the ability to transmit a signal based on another signal.

The data cell has two input-output paths, that work in both directions, a top path and a bottom path.

The top path is a one-input-one-output redstone connection.

The bottom path only transmits redstone if the top path has redstone.

If the top path is tuned off before the bottom path, the bottom output will produre a signal until the top path is turned back on.

§7§oThis gate lets you time redstone pulses and signals.

The gate has a clock input, a reset input, a running output, and an end output.

The clock for the state cell can be changed by right clicking.

When signal enters the clock input, the running output will produce a redstone signal for the amount of seconds specified in the clock. 

At the end of the specified time, the end output will pulse.

The state cell can be reset with a signal from the reset side.

The reset input is the side with the clock hand.

The clock input is the side with a redstone line that's next to the clock hand.

The running output is the side with a redstone line that's opposite to the clock hand.

The end output is the side with a redstone torch.

§7§oThis gate can act as a one-input-one-output redstone connection if signal is coming in from one of the sides with the vertical wire.

It acts as a one-input-three-outputs connection if signal is coming in from the other two sides.
§7§oThis display will let you see what colors are active in a bundled line.

§7§oThis gate lets you cut connections through bundled cables.

By default, the transceiver prevents signals grom going through.

Redstone from the sides with redstone lines can allow signals in the directions specified by the red squares and gray rectangles.

The direction goes red square -> gray rectangle.
§7§oEach of the lamps on this gate works like a lever, that can activate and deactivate different colors from within a bundled cable.

§7§oThis gate works like the randomizer, but it will produce the same signal on all output sides, as opposed to different signals on all sides.

§7§oWhile reciving a redstone signal from its input side, this gate produces random redstone pulses §7§ofrom all other sides.

Right click with a screwdriver to activate or deactivate each output.

§7§oThis gate counts redstone pulses, and lets you do arithmetic!

Right click the gate to change its settings.

The side with a redstone channel and a plus sign will add a configurable amount to the block state.

The side with a redstone channel and a minus sign will subtract a configurable amount to the block state.

When the state is zero, the gate will output a redstone signal from the zero side, the side with a redstone torch and a minus sign.

When the state reaches a maximum, the gate will output a redstone signal from the max side, the side with a redstone torch and a plus sign.

§7§oThis gate works like an AND gate that saves state over time.

The output side is the one with a torch. The side opposite to it is the reset, and the two sides with the square lamps are the inputs.

If one of the inputs receives a signal, the corresponding light will turn on.

The output will produce a pulse after both lights are turned on.

If a redstone signal is applied to the reset side, it will turn off both lights.

§7§oThis gate works like an AND gate, but it can also mantain one of the input signals.

The output is the side with the taller torch.

The strong input is the side with the shorter torch.

The top line connects the other two sides.

The top line can act as a redstone line, transmitting signals to the other side.

If both the strong input, and either side of the strong line are on, the output will be on.

§7§oThis gate lets you invert signals, while still mantaining the input signal.

The top line inverts the signal of the bottom line.

§7§oModular Routers are blocks capable of performing logistics actions (similar to AE2) for small-scale, short-distance automations.

A router performs actions based on the modules placed in its slots, following a cyclical left-to-right order. Modules prform simple actions like pulling and pushing blocks, or more complex ones like breaking, placing, or launching items.

The target locations for each module can be specified by shift + right clicking them on the desired block space.

Once modules are installed, they can be configured by middle clicking them. This allows to set filters and add augments.

Upgrades can be placed in the corresponding slots in a Modular Router.

§7§oAllows a router to work with fluids.
§7§oLike the sender module, but for multiple inventories. Sorting methods can be specified in the module's settings.
§7§oPlaces blocks in a line depending on redstone signal. Redstone and placing settings can be tweaked.
§7§oWorks like an extruder MK1, but blocks or pattern of blocks can be specified from the module's GUI. It doesn't consume blocks from the modular router buffer.
§7§oMakes routers silent and particle-free.
§7§oPrevents damage from bosses and explosions.

§7§oYou don't want this, but if you wanted it...

§7§oHeart of the networks you want to create, works like a visual code chart that lets you place modules down and have them connect to diferent modules. To make the most basic A to B program you must place a 'trigger' module onto the field, the trigger module is what "runs" the script and it is very tilable to how you'd prefer it to run, such as being triggered every 5 seconds, redstone controlled, etc. 

Cables extend the reach of the manager.  Place them adjacent to all blocks you want to include in your automation to connect them to the Manager.

You can then place a "input" module and tell which machine, tile, chest, etc. and from which side, and the same goes for the output module, using this you can simply have a basic input and output system. 

Here's a list of each manager component and what they do in brief detail:

*create trigger*
A module which starts a chain of modules connected to its bottom. It can be set to trigger every configured second, or by a redstone signal via a "redstone receiver" on the network.

*create input*
A module which sets a chest, tile, machine, etc as a "input" which will remove the item and take it to another.

*create output*
A module which sets a chest, tile, machine, etc as a "output" which will take receiving items attached to input modules or similar to it. 

Both inputs and outputs can be filtered. However you can **RIGHT CLICK** a filtered item in the filter to give extra configurations such as being able to be specific of how many of that one item is meant to be in the output, like a enderio limited item filter. 

*create flow control*
A module which can be used to give one or more 'input' modules multiple outputs. Such as having one input to put coal into the side of a furnace and ore on the top, etc. Click the 'connections' tab to change through diferent styles. The nodes on the flow control work with most other modules too, not just input/outputs.

*create fluid input & fluid output*
Works identially to input and output modules, except with fluids to tanks. Can be used to specify how much you want of a fluid to go into the output as well. 

*Auto crafter*
Lets you craft with the command! Just use the module to build the vanilla crafting table recipe you want to use when triggered. You can even set a "Excess" chest which will put excess crafting outputs if the final craft it can fit into it makes excess. AND it stores things such as buckets that are used.

*Sign updater*
Lets you update a sign with prewritten text when triggered. Can have specific parts of the sign updated or not to keep blank spaces or text meant to stay there.

*Camoflauge*
Lets you update a cable camouflage block to look like another when triggered.


---
Advanced:

*condition*
Conditions are powerful modules that when triggered do a true/false check. It can check to see if a inventory its set to watch as any or a single item within a filter you set. If what was set is true it will go to the left' true' prong, and vice versa to the right one if false. This lets you set up different chains of modules to happen if a single chest does or doesn't have a specific item.

*redstone emitter*
creates a module that has to be attached to a "redstone emitter" block which is attached to the manager, allowing it to create a redstone pulse in any configurable side, type and style.

*redstone condition*
Creates a module that has to be attached to a "redstone receiver" block which is attached to the manager. It creates a true/false statement like the normal condition, however it looks for the configured redstone type. Such as strengh, side, etc. Allowing you to have something that works when something only has redstone. (Note you can set a trigger module to also be controlled by a redstone receiver)

*Variables*
Lets you set conditions and collections of blocks that are part of the network as a predetermined color. For example you can have multiple output chests all set to a single variable of the color blue. And then using that, you can have a trigger > input > output setup instead choose to output to the variable of blue.  You can then have this variable in the corner of the setup, as it doesn't need to be interacted with when on declaration.

When set to standard instead of declaration. It will gain trigger spots, letting other modules connect to it. This lets you add, remove, or set a block on the network as a variable when the module is triggered.

*for each loop*
Lets you loop between variables to have diferent effects. Its quite confusing, however you can use this to change up basic empty variables to work with defined variables

*Group*
Lets you compress multiple modules into a singular one. Must be used in junction with a group node, which when used inside of a group lets you set up to 5 inputs and 5 output nodes that you can use on the outside of the group to directly interact with it.

*Sign updater*
Lets you update a sign updater block on the network and thus a sign attached to it when triggered.

*Camoflauge*
Lets you update the look of a cable camoflauge block when triggered.

betterquesting:10.desc:8: §7§oBig rabbit hole incoming! The quests following this one are not required to reach the end of the pack, but you may want to complete them for other reasons ;)

I did not expect to encounter Testificates on Pixonia, but here they are!
Acting as an inside group from the Fluix Historians, some agents were able to follow some of the minions of the Meatball Man into Pixonia, and were able to collect intelligence for the sake of their master, the Arbiter. 
What set off the Meatball Man's attack on the Testificates was not the knowledge over Dimensional Shards alone; both beings, after all, commonly got involved in the happenings of many civilizations, one reaping chaos, one bringing order. 
What started it all was the implication behind this knowledge, a truth that the Arbiter was supposed to keep secret. Thanks to what was taught to the Testificates, though, the Meatball Man was able to piece it together, and driven by desire, he came into Terra, and caused the conflict that I am now fighting.
Given the knowledge of these agents, I thought of asking them what had happened to the Arbiter when they fought back, and what the Meatball Man may want to get out of me; as in the case of my prior encounters with the Fluix Historians, no replies, just oddly specific questions.
Sure, whenever I entered Terra there was a Solar Eclipse, but why does it matter?

Many dungeons use command blocks here, so it is recommended to do this as it helps to declutter the chat.

§7§oExposes the ENTIRETY of your AE2 network's contents to item or fluid transfer.

If not filtered, these can be quite laggy, but they can be used for subnetting.
§7§oNothing to see here, this and the following quests do not exist, and are a figment of your imagination.

§7§oThe space chamber is the most versatile way to automatically place large structures.

To copy a shape to be automatically built, place Space Chamber Corner Blocks in 7 of the 8 corners of the structure you want built, and the Controller in the 8th and final corner.

Right click the controller with a Wrench to set the structure.

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The mark of the Meatball Man has lots of symbolism that is related to gluttony, so I guess I should not be surprised that one of his minions is a gambling-addicted monster.
Still, I did not expect my fighting to get to gambling...

§7§oWell, you decided to go down the rabbit hole, good for you.

To complete this crafting chain, you will have to upgrade large portions of your base. 
For many things, there are going to be alternative recipes, use JEI to search for them; some may require to set up new automations.
For some things, there are going to be multiblock upgrades, which will be listed as optional retrieval objectives.

betterquesting:10.name:8: This is what it's all about!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
§7§oWith regards to LordRaine

§fWho knew grinding balls were musical instruments in bee culture! The melodic bee is a maestro and artisan of the highest caliber: don't tell the bees we're using their musical instruments to kill gods. Or maybe do, they might enjoy that.
§7§oThis chain is just quite great for energy!

A lone Testificate seems to have gone on after the campaign on Furatto. Acting by himself, one of the faithful of the Arbiter has followed the guide of some bees, and was able to reach Lyndenwyrm, gathering knowledge about the power of Entropy after studying the Chaos Dragons in the Sky of Terra.
This agent was one of the Arbiter's inner circle back on Terra, a powerful magician and alchemist, and the creator of the Withers. These six creatures, created from the undead of the Meatball Man, were put in place as the ultimate defense of Terra, and would awaken if the full corporeal form of the Lord of Gluttony were to ever set foot in the land of the Testificates.
As they told me of their mission and research, one interesting detail about powerful recursion came up. 
Fractallite powers have strict rules; no more and no less than one individual can hold a given fractallite power; if a fractallite being dies, their power and their mission become available for the taking. 
One can ascend before gaining powers, as the process of ascension simply consists of reaching a level of attunement to recursion that allows one to sense the fields for these immense powers.
Because of this, there are powerful fractallite beings that hold no powers, and who are simply fighting or waiting to take control over a specific one.

I am not the only one who came to this conclusion. It seems like, in one way or another, I may be fated to take the Arbiter's place and Fractallite power.
One of the faithful of the arbiter has approached me, and told me the Fluix Historians are ready to support me in my struggle against the Meatball Man.
They gave a fabrial, one that would be able to set off the full might of the Withers against the Meatball Man.
This is all nice and good, I think I know what I am doing here, but it leaves the matter of Alchemy, and my own state as the 'chosen one', open.
What sort of plan put me where I am now? I was simply a greedy scientist looking for fame. What about me put me on this journey that was clearly laid out by design.

§7§oAfter copying a given structure, the Copy-Paste gadget works with a Mechanical User.

This works with relatively small structures, and it cannot place some blocks because of a mod limitation.

§7§oThe mob cannot be damaged through normal ranged and melee weapons (things like Zenith and Kikoku can do damage but will not produce drops). Magic damage, Electroblob spells, the railgun, and other magic weapons will work!

§7§oRockets and space stations are cool, but unfortunately sometimes they bug out.
For those that do not want to deal with the possible issues from using Advanced Rocketry, there's the Bee Stargate! A bit of rocketry will still be required, but it'd be a one-time thing!

§fWow, of course Bees have developed extremely advanced Wormhole technology. I love the Bees!
Stepping through a Stargate, that feels quite cool, I will not deny it...
It seems like these structures play an important role in the history, tradition, and culture of Bees. Those that are capable of producing components for these Stargates appear to be highly regarded by the rest of the Bees. This reminds me of how priests and monks are treated by humans. I wonder if their religion has something to do with Stargates...
§7§oCable clusters let you combine multiple blocks that connect to the manager into one.
§7§oThese terminals work like the ME crafting terminal, but for Extended Crafting :)
§7§oGet your hands on some materials from the third mythic shell.

§7§oWelcome to Chapter 10!

This is the end-game! You made it!
§7§oIf you actually want to go through with this, I strongly suggest to start leveling up your Inquiring Matter production, and to upgrade all the multiblocks and recipes that you can.

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
§7§oDimlets are used to control the properties of the custom dimensions created using RFTools Dimensions.

Dimlets are either found as loot in particular RFTools Dimensions, or are crafted in a Dimlet Workbench using materials dropped by Dimlet Parcels.

There are many types of Dimlets, that allow to control biomes, liquids, materials, mobs, sky properies, structure generation, terrain type, features, time cycles, effects, weather in your custom Dimensions.

In order to progress, some specific liquids and materials are made exclusive to these dimensions.

To craft some (most) Dimlets in the Workbench, Absorbers are required. While the absorbers part of progression have their own custom recipes, the 'normal' ones require in-world crafting to be configured.

Material Absorber: place 128 blocks adjacent, they will be consumed

Liquid Absorber: place 128 buckets adjacent, they will be consumed

Biome Absorber: place in the desired biome

Terrain Absorber: place in the dimension with the desired tarrain type (end islands, nether, etc)

Feature Absorber: place in the dimension with the desired feature type (ore veins, caves, etc); some features are exclusive to some custom RFTools Dimensions, so you may want to generate random ones

Time Absorber: trigger with a redstone pulse at the desired time for 10 consecutive days (can be cheated with a timer and time in a bottle)
§7§oLeft click bedrock at the bottom of the overworld using an Awakened Kamium Pickaxe

§7§oTo create custom dimensions with RFTools, you start with an Empty Dimension Tab.

While the tab alone can create custom dimensions, it will do so at random, with cool-looking, but often useless results (you may still want to do it a few times). To start a random Dimension, place the Tab in the Dimension Enscriber, and press 'Store'.

To control the contents of these Dimensions, you can use a Dimension Enscriber to add Dimlets to a Dimension. For more info on Dimlets, check their respective JEI info box (search 'custom dimlets' in JEI).

To activate the Custom Dimension, place it in a Dimension Builder. It will consume the displayed amount of energy to remain active. As long as the dimension has energy, it is accessible. You do not want to be in a dimension if it runs out of energy. Bad things will happen.

To teleport to your custom Dimension, you can use a Dialing Device to link a Matter Transmitter nearby to the desired dimension.

§7§oThe Taxcollector bee will produce the drops of nearby mobs. This will be used in some specific farms.

To reduce the entity lag from the mobs used in these farms, a boat and a passifier syringe can be used to reduce mob AI.

§7§oLetting you know now; from this point forward, puzzles may involve some hidden chests and loot.

There are a variety of methods that can help you find these, a few are listed here...

§7§oLeft click the pickaxe on the bedrock at the bottom of the overworld to create a portal to the bedrock dimension.

The bedrock here can only be broken using the Kamium pickaxe.

§fOut of all the strange artifacts I have encountered in my journey of Thaumaturgy, a pickaxe capable of generating wormholes is the last thing I imagined.
Kamium, this strange and powerful material, rather than being permeated with vis or aura, seems to possess a different type of force, something that sounds familiar, and yet I have no idea what it is.
The wormhole opened by this artifact is fairly mundane, it is solely composed of hard bedrock, with large veins of minerals. I guess it could be useful for someone that is more resource-starved than I am.

I am still not fully sure of what happened exactly, but someone among the Faithful of the Arbiter studied the power of deraddread, and was able to cleanse from its origin it in some way. Again, I may be piecing together things that are not connected, but dread beings seem quite similar to Withers; undead capable of independent will, and yet capable of serving a greater purpose on their own.
